← SOLSTICE PROJECT NOTES

Solstice GXP baffle options — fabrication prototypes

These are estimated prototypes, not confirmed drop-in parts or an engine-use release. The CAD and cut files are real and reproducible. Hidden pan/pickup geometry and mounting coordinates are not established. Do not order a finished kit or install it in an engine from these files without completing the fit work below.

Current generated numeric summary: CURRENT_DIMENSIONS.md. Each parameter’s source and uncertainty: DIMENSION_REGISTER.csv. Rebuild through the single check command in STATUS.md.

P3 next decisions: interface evidence and uncertainty, quantified tolerance sensitivity, and ranked measurement/bench plan. These guide the next fitted revision; the current geometry remains nominal.

A step.parts EMR-201 search returned zero matches; no supplier STEP was found. V2 movement will be illustrative only.

Files and fabrication intent

  • Each file in DXF/ is a single distinct flat profile, at 1:1 millimetres, with closed CUT geometry and no pre-applied kerf compensation. Use the variant quantities in BOM.csv; do not order all eleven profiles for one option.
  • All structure, hinge cheeks and mounting blanks: bare 304 stainless, SendCutSend SST-048, nominal 1.2192 mm / .048 in.
  • V3 leaf only: bare 304 stainless SST-030, nominal 0.762 mm / .030 in. Small parts/thin leaves require manual finishing; do not assume vendor deburring availability.
  • No press-brake operations are specified. The cage and V3 hinge cheeks require owner jigging and TIG welding. Welding is to the removable insert, not the aluminum pan. Small flat plates are manufacturable; a finished hinged assembly is not a laser-cut product.
  • The five 45 × 20 mm blanks are intentionally undrilled and unpositioned. They are transfer-fit stock, not proof of a solved mounting interface. Their reach and thickness may need changing once boss heights and the stock-cover stack are measured.
  • Round pins cannot be laser cut from sheet. V3 uses nominal 3.175 mm stainless rod/solid pins with permanent heads at both ends; the CAD heads are an envelope for owner forming, not a catalog part. Choose compatible stock and a qualified retention process. No loose clips/nuts are specified inside the sump.

The fabrication research records early recommendations, not the final drawing: this prototype uses butt-jig welding (no tabs/slots), 14 × 14 mm fixed cheeks, 3.6 mm bores, and moving-arm contact against the wall as its opening stop. The final wall is 46 mm high, replacing the earlier 35 mm concept assumption. Neither height is verified against the OEM cavity. Small cheek size meets the cited cutting envelope but does not establish weld or fatigue strength.

Coordinate system and assumptions

Origin is the centre of the cage bottom plane. +Z points upward; the relieved tube side is -Y. These axes are not registered to the actual car.

The DXF exporter translates profiles to its own planar origin. Use dimensions relative to the cut boundary, not the drawing origin, to locate features. No scaling or geometry change is implied by that translation.

Fit and assembly sequence

  1. Confirm the actual pan is the factory configuration associated with 12601240, and its cover is 12578196. The sources show five cover bolts. Keep the factory stamped cover and press-fit pickup screen. Do not remove the screen to accommodate this concept.
  2. Make a full-size nonmetal mock-up from the DXFs before buying cut stainless. Establish actual pickup/screen envelope, floor contour, floor-to-cover heights, all five boss coordinates/heights, dipstick/drain/return paths, and installation/removal path. The top frame DXF is a useful footprint template, not a complete fit test.
  3. Resize frame, partitions, tube relief and wall-bottom profiles to those observations. Keep a small controlled bottom clearance without hard contact; no clearance value is approved here. Do not seal a trapped cavity that cannot refill or drain. At only 1 mm gap, the nominal 560 mm outer perimeter already presents roughly 560 mm² of bypass—similar to one V3 window. This estimate is a warning about sensitivity, not a flow calculation.
  4. Transfer the verified bosses to the five mounting blanks; determine any required stand-offs. Retain the original cover height, bolt engagement, seating, and rotating-assembly clearance. If the proposed blanks cannot do this, redesign them. Do not simply stack them under stock bolts and assume the original torque remains applicable.
  5. Dry-fit and tack the cage in a jig. Verify dimensions before final welding. For V1, the divider ends meet the front/rear portions of the top frame. For V2/V3, four walls butt together and meet the top frame. Finish and inspect welded joints; remove all dross, abrasive residue and debris.
  6. V2: fit actual EMR-201 doors on the chamber side following the supplier diagram, using solid rivets and the manufacturer procedure. Allow at least the specified 25.4 mm swing space to the pickup, then check the actual door. The supplier intentionally permits a slightly open rest position for refill.
  7. V3: jig fixed cheeks perpendicular to the wall. Weld each moving cheek to the inner leaf face over its 14 mm edge (Z10–24 mm), avoiding distortion of the .762 mm sheet. The broad inward arm is intentional. Use a coupon first; reject a distorted or weak joint. Bore alignment and free rotation must be checked after welding.
  8. Fit pins and form permanent retention while maintaining free axial movement. The nominal CAD provides .3 mm head-to-fixed-cheek clearance on each side. Do not upset a pin against the moving cheeks. Check the broad closed seat and both arm stops, deburr the contact edges, and verify free motion after retention and mounting.
  9. Bench-check refill/drain behavior and operation with the intended oil over operating temperature. Then verify pressure under controlled conditions before claiming oil-control benefit. No flow, thermal, fatigue, wear or vehicle test has been performed here.

What has been checked

review/validation.json records checks against the saved STEP and DXF files: positive valid solids, declared stock thicknesses, units, CUT-only loops, profile bounds, supplier mounting-hole geometry, stationary intersections, sampled V3 movement in 5° increments, reverse seat and 60° opening-stop behavior. V2 commercial proxies are excluded from clearance certification. Snapshots were generated for each part and assembly; see review/.

Successful CAD and supplier-format checks do not establish pan fit, reliable lubrication, final order acceptance or engine-use suitability. Current source comparison is in research/fabrication.md; exact selected material records and dated supplier feeds are retained.

Rebuild

From the project root, run python below through:

uvx --no-config --managed-python --python 3.13 --from cadgen==0.7.21 python

Build the selected assembly source under src/; build its <part>_cut.py scripts for the quantities in BOM.csv. checks/rebuild.py is the explicit complete-package rebuild. Then run checks/validate.py. Keep each STEP with its sibling .step.json when present; that file contains native motion/material data.

Animations and standards

Each option includes a six-second MP4 and an animated GLB with a demo clip. REFERENCE_BOARD.html plays all three locally; ANIMATION/ holds videos and GLB/ holds portable animated 3D files. V1 separates its three assembly pieces for explanation. V2 rotates simplified purchased-door leaf proxies; it does not establish the supplier hardware's shape or actual rest angle. V3 rotates each leaf and its two attached cheeks inward from 0° to 60° and back, with the pins and fixed frame stationary. All gates move together only to make the mechanism easy to see. Real doors respond independently to local oil and acceleration. Six seconds is arbitrary presentation timing, not a predicted opening or closing response.

QUALITY.md defines design, modelling and production standards. review/quality-assessment.md is the independent Astra Medium review; review/FINAL_QA.md records final build and playback closure without rewriting that review's historical evidence. All physical-release holds remain visible.

Complete geometry and animation rebuild commands, from the project root:

uvx --no-config --managed-python --python 3.13 --from cadgen==0.7.21 python checks/rebuild.py
uvx --no-config --managed-python --python 3.13 --from cadgen==0.7.21 python checks/render_animations.py
python3 checks/build_board.py
python3 checks/package_delivery.py

The last command verifies current files, writes SHA-256 manifests and packages this project. It does not run the geometry kernel; run the geometry rebuild first after source edits. Existing still posters are retained as inspected presentation images; the animation renderer produces fresh 0/1.5/3-second review stills.

P1 continuation — process coupon and continuous roof check

The full variants retain their reviewed geometry. A separate STEP/v3_hinge_coupon.step now reuses one existing V3 wall/gate for bench process trials. Use COUPON_PLAN.md, COUPON_BOM.csv, COUPON_RESULTS.csv and PDF/hinge_inspection_drawing.pdf; the coupon has six cut pieces plus one pin and introduces no new cut profiles. It has no roof or pan mounts and is not an engine part.

The new analytical roof-height bound is 1.577794898 mm at 43.897886°, slightly tighter than the earlier sampled 1.580463 mm. TOLERANCE_BUDGET.md distinguishes this nominal geometric gap from the unqualified weld/stock/thermal/deflection stack. The drawing is a nominal inspection document, not a production drawing with approved tolerances. STATUS.md is the authoritative resumption entry point.
